page.overview:
What is Orient Expedition?

The theme is about Johnny Thunder, Dr. Kilroy, Pippin Reed, and their new Asian friends going through Asia to find the Golden Dragon of Marco Polo and his three other treasures before the sneaky Lord Sam Sinister and his partners-in-crime did. The story is told through comics included in building instructions, magazines, and LEGO.com. It is unique in that every set above 100 pieces came with stat cards and/or a piece of a game board that could be added to the Orient Expedition Board Game to maximize fun.

The idea of an India subtheme for Adventurers goes back to at least 1996, with concept art of what would become Johnny Thunder and Dr. Kilroy exploring an Indian jungle. Later, by 2000, the concept of a Silk Road theme had arisen that would feature the Adventurers exploring Arabia, India, Tibet, and China. It is unknown what sets were designed for this iteration of the theme, but a video game in the form of plans for the third LEGO Island game was explored to tie into it. According to the lead designer, this was cancelled alongside the theme because the latter "didn't test well."

The creative team on Orient Expedition included model designer Bjarke Lykke Madsen, project manager João Esteves, and design manager Kim Yde. A LEGO Club interview detailed the behind-the-scenes development of the theme.

After the completion of their goal in the theme and retrieving the legendary silver Horn of Africa, Pippin Reed takes Johnny Thunder to Venice. Dr. Kilroy shows them a piece of an ancient map of Asia with a riddle from Marco Polo. Soon after, Johnny found out that it fit into the other third of a map behind a glass window. The combined map form two things. The first was the story of how upon leaving India, Marco left his Golden Dragon, a gift from the Emperor Kublai Khan, in Khan's palace that can only be unlocked by his three other treasures. The second was the way to the first of Marco Polo's treasures: the golden shield of Marco Polo in the Scorpion Palace, located in India. They head off to India, but Lord Sam Sinister, who had been listening in from outside overheard their chatter and rushed off in his car to give pursuit.
